extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment & Discipline, and legal counsel handling USPTO disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order approving a settlement resolving disciplinary charges against a registered patent practitioner; it states stipulated facts, legal conclusions (rules violated), sanctions, publication requirements, and conditions for reinstatement under USPTO regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction for disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites these statutory and regulatory authorities as the basis for the Office's ability to adjudicate and approve settlement agreements resolving disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable professional conduct rules by date of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the alleged conduct occurred prior to May 3, 2013, the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.) is applicable; as of May 3, 2013, the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101 through 11.901) apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of which code/rules govern alleged misconduct depends on when the conduct occurred; this affects which regulatory provisions are cited for violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) — conduct reflecting adversely on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribing engaging in any other conduct that adversely reflects on a practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order finds Respondent violated §10.23(b)(6) based on specified conduct (including being suspended by another tribunal); cross-reference to §10.23(c)(5) (suspension by another authority) is made as the basis for the adverse reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5) — suspension by other authority as adverse reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribing being suspended from the practice of law by any duly constituted authority of a State or the United States; such suspension is conduct that can adversely reflect on fitness to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifically cites the Respondent's suspension from the U.S. Bankruptcy Court as triggering §10.23(c)(5) and thus supporting a §10.23(b)(6) violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(a) — competence to handle matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribing handling a matter which the practitioner is not competent to handle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order finds Respondent violated §10.77(a) by filing Chapter 11 bankruptcy cases without possessing the requisite skill; competence (or lack thereof) to handle a class of matters is a basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension sanction (term and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters for two (2) years commencing nunc pro tunc from January 10, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sanction specifies both duration and the scope (patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters) and ties the effective date to the prior court order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued suspension until reinstatement petition granted (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall remain suspended from practice before the Office until the OED Director grants a petition reinstating Respondent pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement requires following the procedures in §11.60; the Order makes reinstatement discretionary upon a properly granted petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition for reinstatement — retake and pass registration examination (37 C.F.R. § 11.60(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director's granting of any petition for reinstatement for Respondent to practice before the Office in patent matters is additionally predicated upon Respondent retaking and passing the Examination for Registration to Practice in Patent Cases Before the USPTO pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As an express condition of reinstatement for patent practice, the practitioner must retake and pass the patent bar exam; this is a reinstatement eligibility criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 as a term of the Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires compliance but does not restate §11.58; practitioners must consult §11.58 for the specific obligations imposed during/after suspension (e.g., notice, handling of client matters).

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director publication obligations (37 C.F.R. § 11.59 and reading room posting)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the OED Reading Room and comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59; publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided Notice of Suspension text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order prescribes public notice steps: posting in the electronic Reading Room and publishing a specified-form notice in the Official Gazette; §11.59 governs public disclosure of disciplinary actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining a USPTO Customer Number while suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an administrative restriction tied to the suspension status to prevent practice/filings before reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement/Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding in: (1) addressing further complaints of same/similar misconduct; (2) any future disciplinary proceeding against Respondent as an aggravating factor or to rebut representations; and/or (3) connection with any request for reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order preserves the Office's ability to use the record both substantively (aggravating/rebuttal) and procedurally (reinstatement review) in future actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties bear their own costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement and this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement terms include allocation of costs—no award of costs between the parties under this Agreement/Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content/form of Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Official Gazette notice must be materially consistent with the Notice of Suspension text included in the Order, describing the respondent, registration number, violations (specific regulatory citations), suspension term, and reinstatement condition (retaking/passing the examination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order provides verbatim text to be used as the basis for the public notice, indicating the level of detail and the specific regulatory citations that must be reflected in the published notice.
